scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Nangiar koothu is an offshoot of the ancient Sanskrit drama tradition of Kutiyattam, with a documented history spanning 1,500 years.
It was traditionally performed by the Nangyaramma women of the Ambalavasi Nambiar community in Kerala, though this exclusivity ended in the late 20th century.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The performance is dedicated to narrating the life of Lord Krishna, drawing specifically from the text Sree Krishna Charitam.
Today it is a living tradition.

The drum provides the rhythmic and sonic backdrop for the performer's movements.
The music is defined by the resonant, deep tones of the mizhavu, a pot drum that provides the rhythmic pulse for the performer's narrative.
